findings.message: Index out of bounds panic: accessing log.Topics[i] without checking if i < len(log.Topics) before the loop, even though there's a prior check for len(l.pbFilter.Topics) > len(log.Topics), the loop iterates over l.pbFilter.Topics and accesses log.Topics[i] where i can exceed log.Topics length if len(l.pbFilter.Topics) == len(log.Topics) but some early topics are skipped due to nil/empty entries.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit bounds check before accessing log.Topics[i]: if i >= len(log.Topics) { return false } inside the loop before target := log.Topics[i]

fixes.explanation: Added explicit bounds check before accessing log.Topics[i] to prevent index out of bounds panic when len(l.pbFilter.Topics) == len(log.Topics) but early topics are skipped due to nil/empty entries.

findings.message: Index out of bounds panic: accessing log.Topics[i] without checking if i < len(log.Topics) inside the loop. The prior check `if len(l.pbFilter.Topics) > len(log.Topics)` only catches cases where filter topics are strictly longer, but does not prevent i from exceeding len(log.Topics) when some filter topics are skipped (nil or empty) and log has fewer topics than filter entries.

verdict.summary: The reviewer repeatedly reported the same finding across 4 rounds without verifying the fix, and the coder correctly rejected it each time by pointing out the existing bounds check. This indicates the reviewer failed to read the code or understand the fix, wasting cycles and reducing confidence in the review process. No actual bugs were found or fixed.
recommendations: Reviewer must read the actual code and prior fixes before re-reporting findings
Implement automated diff-checking to detect unchanged code and skip redundant findings
Add a 'verified_fix' flag or CI integration to confirm fixes before re-reporting
